title: Highly Improved Captures of the Diamondback Moth, Plutella xylostella, Using Bimodal Traps
content: Many cases have been described where the combination of semiochemicals and light sources in traps results in a significant increase in insect adult attraction. In this context, we tested four different baits using Delta plastic traps to catch DBM adults: (1) dispensers containing DBM SSA; (2) UV (365-370 nm) LEDs; (3) a combination of a dispenser containing DBM SSA and LEDs (SSA + LED); and (4) no lures (Control). The trials were conducted in Northwestern Russia (the vicinity of St. Petersburg) during 2022–2024 on cabbage crops. The results showed a highly significant interaction between SSA and LED with respect to their attractiveness to male DBM adults, as evidenced by an average 15-fold increase in DBM captures after the traps containing SSA were equipped with a second lure, LED. The article discusses the prospects for using the identified synergistic effect of interaction between SSA and LED to enhance the catch of DBM adults for practical purposes, such as improving monitoring and developing more effective mass trapping technologies.
